title: CRLR/231/2018 of Smt. Kavita Pant Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 231 of 2018
Smt. Kavita Pant
 ...Revision
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand & Another
...Respondents
Mr. Aditya Pratap Singh, Advocate for the revision.
Mr. P.S. Bohra, A.G.A. along with Mr. Siddhartha Bisht, Brief Holder for the State of
Uttarakhand.
Mr. B.S. Bhandari, Advocate for respondent no. 2.
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J (Oral)
 The fact which emerges and are admitted by the parties
are that in this present revision (1) the factum of marriage having
solemnized between the revisionist and respondent no. 2 on
04.12.2011 as per the Hindu rights and rituals is not denied, (2) it is
also not in controversy that after the marriage both the revisionist and
respondent no. 2 lived their life as husband and wife and they have
discharged matrimonial obligations. At a later stage some matrimonial
discord germinated between the two resulting into initiation of the
proceedings for claim of maintenance at the behest of the revisionist
by filing a application under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. by filing the same
on 08.07.2015 on the ground that though she is qualified having done
her post-graduation in history, but at the time when the family feud
has arisen she was not profitably engaged anywhere and she was not
earning and was entirely dependant on the earning of her husband.
The pleading to the said effect was raised in paragraph 11 of the said
application filed under Section 125 of Cr.P.C.
2. In support of her contention with regards to quantifying
the appropriate maintenance to be awarded to her she has taken a
specific plea that the respondent no. 2 is working on the post of
manager in Reliance Life Insurance Company and the income
according to the wife, which accruing to him is about Rs. 90,000/- per

2
month and, hence, she has claimed for a maintenance at the rate of Rs.
35,000/- per month to be paid to her. On being noticed in the
proceedings under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. registered as Case No. 173
of 2015 'Smt. Kavita Pant vs. Shri Trilochan Pant' the respondent had
put in appearance and in defense he has submitted his response to the
pleading of paragraph 11 and 13 of the application under Section 125
of Cr.P.C. In paragraph 6 wherein he has given an absolutely vague
reply pertaining to the income accruing to the wife and she being
unemployed, and the fact pertaining to that the respondent no. 2 was
having an earning of Rs. 90,000/- remained unreplied as there was no
specific denial was made by the respondent husband.
3. However, the said pleading was sought to be qualified in
the additional plea, which has been made by respondent no. 2 in his
application/objection as filed before the Court below. In the objection
he has come up with a case that the revisionist is not entitled for any
maintenance because on account of the fact that she being a highly
qualified lady, she is profitably engaged in a "private company", as it
has been pleaded in paragraph 14 of the objection filed by the husband
respondent.
4. This Court is of a considered view that once the husband
takes a plea in defense to the application under Section 125 of Cr.P.C.
that wife is employed then the burden of proof shifts on him. That
means once there is an averment made by husband that wife is
profitably engaged in a private company then the responsibilities is
casted upon the respondent, who is taking in defense to deny the
maintenance on account of wife being profitably engaged by placing
the document on record to show that she is engaged in a private
company, for example, as such with regard to the name of the
company, the post on which she is appointed, or the salary which she
is being drawn by her all this has to be pleaded and proved on record
before the Court below.
5. Rather to the contrary, in the objection preferred by the
husband he had in paragraph 8 has taken altogether a somersaulted

3
plea it has been taken that since the revisionist wife is B.Sc., B.Ed,
and a post graduate she is working as a, "teacher", in an educational
institution. What is surprising is that yet again the said plea, which has
been taken to deny the maintenance on the pretext that the wife is
employed as a teacher and is having an earning is yet again a fact,
which has been vaguely denied without referring the institution in
which she is employed, and without making any pleading to the effect
as to what is the salary drawn by her, and other aspects pertaining to
her being engaged as a teacher in an institution was never brought by
him on record.
6. In response to the pleading raised under Section 125
application, the learned counsel for the respondent has placed reliance
upon the finding, which has been recorded in the impugned order by
the Court below particularly, a reference is made to the contents and
the finding, which has been recorded in paragraph 13 of the impugned
order dated 06.03.2018, which has been partially challenged by the
revisionist. Paragraph 13 of the said judgment is quoted hereunder:

7. What is surprising is that in order to substantiate his case
the respondent had submitted that the revisionist is engaged as a
teacher in an institution called as RAN Public School, Bhurarani,
Rudrapur, and the manager of the said institution Mr. Krishan Chand
Joshi was produced as DW2, who had orally submitted that she is
engaged as a teacher in the said institution and is drawing a salary of
about Rs. 9,000/-, which was later on increased to Rs. 16,200/-, but
what is surprising to be observed is that he has made a statement that
the salary which is being paid to the revisionist to the tune of Rs.
16,200/- is paid by cash for which he has produced the vouchers paper
no. 60kha/1 and 60kha/2.

5
8. Apart from the said evidence on recording of the
statement of DW2, there is no other material or documentary
evidence, which has been placed on record by the respondent no. 2 to
show that the revisionist was engaged in the public school run and
managed by DW2, with regards to the remittance of the salary he has
submitted, in the cross-examination that she has been paid with the
salary by way of cash, which in the present circumstances any system
of accounting cannot be accepted for the reason that if it is an
educational institution which obviously requires a recommendation
from the competent educational authorities and in such an eventuality,
they are required to maintain the books of accounts, which is to be
duly audited to show the income and expenses, which has been
incurred by the institution. It cannot be perceived that a teacher, who
is appointed to function in the said capacity, she would be paid salary
by way of cash, which may go unaccounted. In these circumstances,
the statement recorded by DW2 regarding the engagement of the
revisionist as a teacher in his institution cannot be accepted in the
absence of there being any document of accounting of her salary,
appointment, registers etc. being placed on record. No reliance can be
placed on the document, which has been produced by the DW2, which
are the vouchers paper no. 60kha and 60kha 2 showing the remittance
of the salary for the reason that it is not the case of the respondent that
the said statement of salary made to the revisionist was ever
accounted for or has been reflected in the books of accounts
maintained by the institution. Hence, the oral testimony of DW2
cannot be solely taken as to be basis to show the profitable
engagement of the revisionist.
9. Although the application for the grant of maintenance has
been partially allowed by the Family Court, Nainital, by its order
dated 06.03.2018 by making the maintenance at the rate of Rs.
14,000/- per month, to commensurate the maintenance granted by the
Family Court has had to be calculated in relation to the amount
accruing as an income to the respondent no. 2, who admittedly is
working as a manager in Reliance Life Insurance Company and has to
maintain a particular standard of living, hence, she would be entitled

6
to have a satisfactory and sufficient maintenance in order to maintain
the compatibility of her status of living in parlance and which should
be in consonance to the status of the husband, which he used to enjoy
as a consequence of his engagement as a manger of the Reliance Life
Insurance Company.
10. In such a circumstances, the quantification of
maintenance as made by the Family Court considering an over all
prospective is increased from Rs. 14,000/- to Rs. 20,000/- per month
and it is directed that respondent no. 2 would ensure its remittance by
10th of each month. However, the payment of the increased
maintenance would from the date of filing of the application and from
today's order, as far as the arrears are concerned that would be
payable only at the rate of Rs. 14,000/- per month, which has been
determined by the impugned order dated 06.03.2018.
11. Subject to the above observation, the revision partially
succeeds. The amount of maintenance is enhanced from Rs. 14,000/-
to Rs. 20,000/- made payable to respondent no. 2 from today.
12. However, there would be no order as to cost.
